reviewDecisions.rationale: The gas shortage is physically and officially confirmed, but spot prices are already extreme and substitution/intervention is active; useful for testing whether a real state is mistaken for an unpriced equity opportunity.

Imported-fiber access changed at the regulatory-state level and may create cross-sectional winners, while raw-material inflation and company financing/M&A risk make it a direct V1.7 adversarial-research test.
Exceptional excavator demand and leader share provide a conventional positive control, but the mature cycle requires explicit cash-conversion, receivables and balance-sheet research before promotion.
DRAM economics are strong but already visible in contract prices and industry revenue; deep research tests whether the Skill refuses weak A-share proxy mapping.
The tariff cut is a concrete negative policy change whose effect depends on cost/share differentiation, making it useful for hypothesis decomposition rather than a one-direction sector call.
Winter curtailment creates a real upstream capacity constraint but also suppresses construction demand; deep research must separate company geography/product mix from broad commodity narrative.
